ticket.title: Keep newly added relationship rows correctly associated
ticket.text:
Keep newly added relationship rows correctly associated

## Impact

When multiple relationships are added, removing one row can cause another row to display a relationship type that does not match its Formik value.

## Affected code

- `packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/section/patient-relationships/relationships-section.component.tsx`
- `packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/patient-registration.types.ts`
- `packages/esm-patient-registration-app/src/patient-registration/section/patient-relationships/relationships-section.test.tsx`

## Root cause

New relationships do not have server UUIDs, but the UUID is used as the React key. Multiple new rows therefore share the same `undefined` key.

The relationship type selector uses `defaultValue`, making it uncontrolled. When React reuses a row after another row is removed, the selector can retain state from the removed row.

## Reproduction

1. Add two new relationship rows.
2. Select a different person and relationship type in each row.
3. Remove the first row.
4. Inspect the remaining row.
5. Its displayed selection may not match its Formik value.

## Expected behavior

Each relationship row should retain its own person and relationship type when other rows are added or removed.

## Implementation direction

Give each new relationship a stable client-side identifier when it is created. Use the server UUID as the key for existing relationships and the client-side identifier for new relationships.

Make the relationship type selector controlled by its Formik value. Do not include the client-side identifier in REST payloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every relationship row has a unique, stable React key.
- The relationship type selector is controlled by Formik.
- Removing one row does not change another row’s displayed or stored values.
- Adding multiple rows produces no duplicate-key warning.
- Add an interaction test that assigns different values to two rows, removes the first, and verifies the second.

Verified against `openmrs-esm-patient-management` commit `c64fb336`.
